title: Three Histories: Life, Mind, and Self-Discovery
hypothesis: Typed records prevent synthetic results from silently becoming biological validation.
exercise: Remove the source kind and ask which claim changes without new measurement.
limit: Record provenance is not source authentication or scientific peer review.
falsifier: A synthetic-only record is marked sufficient biological validation.
control: Incomplete, precise, imprecise, inconsistent and domain-mismatched records
book: A Brief History of the Brain

title: Before Neurons: How Life Maintains Itself
hypothesis: A resource-aware controller sustains more completed work than always-work in the specified toy environment.
exercise: Increase resource inflow or work cost and compare energy balance and useful work.
limit: Arbitrary resource units are not metabolism, entropy, health advice, or evidence of life.
falsifier: Resource-aware completed work does not exceed always-work under the reference environment, or the balance residual is nonzero beyond tolerance.
control: Always-work policy with the same disturbances

title: The Origin of Nervous Systems: From Local Response to Coordination

exercise: Set the gain to zero in a copy and inspect loss of propagation.
limit: Graph recurrence alone does not explain the evolutionary origin of neurons.
falsifier: The reference cycle fails to retain more terminal activity than the chain.
control: Chain versus cycle at identical gain

title: The History of Memory: Retention, Reconstruction, and the Future
